findings.title: Timeout can leave later flusher processes running
findings.body: When the shared join deadline expires while waiting for an earlier process, this `break` skips the remaining processes, including the `terminate()` call below. A later worker blocked in Redis or Kafka can therefore outlive `join(timeout)` and continue producing or accessing Redis during shutdown. Continue through the workers and terminate any that remain alive after the deadline.

findings.title: Reject non-positive flusher process limits
findings.body: The CLI accepts any integer for `--flusher-processes`, but this expression treats `0` as unset (silently allowing one worker per shard) and leaves negative values unchanged. With a negative value, `num_processes` is negative, the process map is empty, and assigning a shard raises `KeyError` during consumer startup. Validate that the limit is positive and only use the shard count when the argument is `None`.

findings.title: The added wait is disabled by the test's sleep monkeypatch
findings.body: This test replaces `time.sleep` with a no-op at line 15, so this call does not give the flusher thread time to observe the updated drift. `step.join()` immediately sets the shared stop flag, and the worker can exit before flushing; the test therefore still has a race and can fail intermittently. Use synchronization that is not patched out, such as an event or a bounded wait on the expected output.
